title: U.S. House · Texas's 12th District
area: Fort Worth and surrounding Tarrant County.

context.text: Incumbent Republican Craig Goldman won his primary unopposed. Heli Rodriguez Prilliman defeated Kenneth Morgan-Aguilera in the Democratic primary, 59.8%-40.2%.

candidates.name: Craig Goldman
candidates.ballotNote: Won the March 3, 2026 Republican primary unopposed

summary.text: Craig Goldman is the Republican incumbent seeking re-election in Texas's 12th District. A fourth-generation Fort Worth native who worked in his family's gourmet food and wine store, he served twelve years in the Texas House before winning the congressional seat in 2024. He serves on the House Energy and Commerce Committee and has introduced legislation with Fort Worth-area Democratic Rep. Marc Veasey, including a bill to designate a post office in memory of former Rep. Kay Granger.

background.text: Born in Texas and lives in Fort Worth. His official biography describes him as a fifth-generation Texan and fourth-generation Fort Worth native.
Earned a B.A. from the University of Texas at Austin.

Spent nearly a decade working alongside his father at the family-run gourmet food and wine store in Fort Worth, according to his official biography; Ballotpedia also lists work on political campaigns and partnerships in several real estate investment companies.
Won election to the Texas House of Representatives, District 97, in 2012 and served from 2013 to 2025, representing part of Tarrant County.
In the Texas House, held leadership positions including chairman of the House Committee on Energy Resources and chairman of the House Republican Caucus, according to his official biography.
Advanced from the March 5, 2024 Republican primary for the open 12th District seat vacated by Rep. Kay Granger, defeated John O'Shea in the May 28, 2024 primary runoff, and won the general election.
Took office in January 2025 and serves on the House Energy and Commerce Committee. His district includes parts of Tarrant and Parker Counties.
In 2026, he and Rep. Marc Veasey (D-TX-33), who also represents Fort Worth, introduced the Kay Granger Post Office Act to designate a post office in memory of the former congresswoman.

positions.summary: His official issues page, describing the One Big Beautiful Bill Act he says he is proud to deliver on, lists nearly $150 billion for border security and deportations plus hiring bonuses for ICE and Border Patrol agents.
positions.quote: Allocates nearly $150 billion to secure our border and facilitate deportations

positions.summary: His official issues page presents the bill's cuts to clean-energy funding and rescission of electric-vehicle mandates as accomplishments.
positions.quote: Cuts billions in handouts for Green New Energy initiatives and groups

positions.summary: His official issues page lists the bill's support for school choice through educational savings accounts among its accomplishments.
positions.quote: Supports school choice through educational savings accounts

record.text: Serves on the Committee on Energy and Commerce, including its Subcommittees on Commerce, Manufacturing, and Trade, Communications and Technology, and Energy, for the 119th Congress (2025-2026).
Introduced the Kay Granger Post Office Act with Democratic Rep. Marc Veasey, who like Goldman represents the Fort Worth area, to designate a post office in honor of former Rep. Kay Granger.
Co-introduced the Stop EU Overreach Act with Reps. Jodey Arrington and Greg Steube, aimed at countering European Union corporate-sustainability regulations affecting American businesses.
Co-introduced a bipartisan Prior Authorization Transparency bill with Reps. August Pfluger, Rob Wittman, Jimmy Panetta, Donald Norcross and Kim Schrier.
Introduced the Better Care, Better Cost Act to implement market-based incentives intended to strengthen Medicaid.

candidates.name: Heli Rodriguez Prilliman
candidates.ballotNote: Won the March 3, 2026 Democratic primary, 59.8%-40.2%, over Kenneth Morgan-Aguilera

summary.text: Angela 'Heli' Rodriguez Prilliman is the Democratic nominee challenging incumbent Craig Goldman in Texas's 12th District. A Fort Worth entrepreneur, she describes a career in the technology startup world and as the founder of a nail salon and online beauty-education company. She has not held elected office and is campaigning on universal health care, universal child care, voting rights and fully funding public schools.

background.text: Raised in Stephenville, Texas; graduated from Stephenville High School in 2005 and earned a bachelor's degree from Texas A&M University in 2009.

According to her campaign website, she is the founder of Lacquerbar and Lacquerbar U, a nail salon and online education startup that she says was venture-backed and was one of the first 24 startups chosen for the inaugural Backstage Capital Accelerator.
Says she was part of the founding team at Fivestars, a software company serving small businesses that, per her website, was acquired by SumUp in late 2021.

Her campaign website says she is an Entrepreneur-in-Residence at the accelerator FourthWave, a founder mentor for the Black Ambition Futurists Program, and co-creator of the podcast The C Curve for nail technicians.
Ballotpedia lists her profession as small business owner; she has not previously held elected office and won the Democratic nomination in the March 3, 2026 primary.
Describes herself as a Fort Worth mom and cites her grandmother, Fort Worth civil rights activist Pauline Gasca Valenciano, as an influence.

priorities.text: Fully funding public schools and removing what she describes as billionaire money from politics.

positions.summary: Campaigns on fighting for universal health care, citing Texas's high rate of uninsured residents.
Lists universal child care among her core campaign issues.
Her campaign Issues page says universal health care and child care would be paid for by taxing billionaires.
positions.quote: I'm advocating for a universal healthcare system and a universal child care system, all paid for by taxing the small group of billionaires who have taken advantage of American workers.
